sections.heading: The legal rule
sections.body:
109. (1) Whoever does any act with such intention or knowledge, and under such circumstances that, if he by that act caused death, he would be guilty of murder, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine; and if hurt is caused to any person by such act, the offender shall be liable either to imprisonment for life, or to such punishment as is hereinbefore mentioned
(2) When any person offending under sub-section (1) is under sentence of imprisonment for life, he may, if hurt is caused, be punished with death or with imprisonment for life, which shall mean the remainder of that person’s natural life

sections.heading: Essential ingredients
sections.body:
(1) Whoever does any act with such intention or knowledge, and under such circumstances that, if he by that act caused death, he would be guilty of murder, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine; and if hurt is caused to any person by such act, the offender shall be liable either to imprisonment for life, or to such punishment as is hereinbefore mentioned
(2) When any person offending under sub-section (1) is under sentence of imprisonment for life, he may, if hurt is caused, be punished with death or with imprisonment for life, which shall mean the remainder of that person’s natural life

sections.heading: Statutory illustrations
sections.body:
(a) A shoots at Z with intention to kill him, under such circumstances that, if death ensued, A would be guilty of murder. A is liable to punishment under this section
(b) A, with the intention of causing the death of a child of tender years, exposes it in a desert place. A has committed the offence defined by this section, though the death of the child does not ensue
(c) A, intending to murder Z, buys a gun and loads it. A has not yet committed the offence. A fires the gun at Z. He has committed the offence defined in this section, and, if by such firing he wounds Z, he is liable to the punishment provided by the latter part of sub-section (1)
(d) A, intending to murder Z by poison, purchases poison and mixes the same with food which remains in A’s keeping; A has not yet committed the offence defined in this section. A places the food on Z’s table or delivers it to Z’s servants to place it on Z’s table. A has committed the offence defined in this section

hypotheticals.question: Whether BNS s. 109 (Attempt to murder) applies, and how structured written arguments should be framed.
hypotheticals.analysis:
Step 1 — Identify the provision. The correct current-law cite is BNS s. 109 (Attempt to murder), Chapter VI — Of Offences Affecting the Human Body.
Step 2 — State the legal test in your own words, then list the ingredients:
   (1) Whoever does any act with such intention or knowledge, and under such circumstances that, if he by that act caused death, he would be guilty of murder, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine; and if hurt is caused to any person by such act, the offender shall be liable either to imprisonment for life, or to such punishment as is hereinbefore mentioned
   (2) When any person offending under sub-section (1) is under sentence of imprisonment for life, he may, if hurt is caused, be punished with death or with imprisonment for life, which shall mean the remainder of that person’s natural life
Step 3 — Check limitations, provisos and the rest of the Chapter so you do not apply s. 109 in a vacuum.
Step 4 — Map each fact to an ingredient. Write “this fact proves ingredient (a)” or “this fact is missing, so the section is not made out”.
Step 5 — Conclude. If every essential ingredient is proved and no exception covers the case, BNS s. 109 applies. If any essential ingredient fails, say so and stop. Do not invent a different section to save the answer.

questionsAndAnswers.question: Legal Assessment & Statutory Note: BNS s. 109 (Attempt to murder)
questionsAndAnswers.answer:
Introduction. BNS s. 109 deals with Attempt to murder. It sits in Chapter VI — Of Offences Affecting the Human Body of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023. After 1 July 2024 this is the current-law citation for this offence / definition / punishment.

Meaning. Attempt to murder (old 307). Doing an act with such intention or knowledge, and under such circumstances, that had death been caused the offender would be guilty of murder.

Legal rule. In student language: BNS s. 109 is the rule on “Attempt to murder”. The section provides that (1) Whoever does any act with such intention or knowledge, and under such circumstances that, if he by that act caused death, he would be guilty of murder, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine; and if hurt is caused to any person by such act, the offender shall be liable either to imprisonment for life, or to such punishment as is hereinbefore mentioned. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Essential ingredients. An authoritative analysis must list them, not hide them in one paragraph:
1. (1) Whoever does any act with such intention or knowledge, and under such circumstances that, if he by that act caused death, he would be guilty of murder, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine; and if hurt is caused to any person by such act, the offender shall be liable either to imprisonment for life, or to such punishment as is hereinbefore mentioned
2. (2) When any person offending under sub-section
3. (1) is under sentence of imprisonment for life, he may, if hurt is caused, be punished with death or with imprisonment for life, which shall mean the remainder of that person’s natural life

Illustrations. The section itself supplies worked examples. In legal analysis, pick one illustration, restate its facts, and show which ingredient it proves. Illustration (a): (a) A shoots at Z with intention to kill him, under such circumstances that, if death ensued, A would be guilty of murder. A is liable to punishment under this section

Limitations. Apply only the conditions written in s. 109. Do not import a defence from a different chapter unless the question requires it.

Consequence / punishment. Up to 10 years + fine; if hurt caused, life or 10 years.

Connected sections. Read with BNS s. 101, BNS s. 62. A preliminary brief mentions the neighbour; comprehensive submissions explain the exact distinction.

Conclusion. BNS s. 109 is the complete current-law heading for Attempt to murder. Define, list ingredients, use an illustration, note any explanation or exception, apply, cite. That is a complete statutory structure.

learningObjectives: Master the elements of attempt to murder under BNS s. 109(1).
Analyze the punishment tiers: up to 10 years and fine for basic attempt, and imprisonment for life or 10 years if hurt is caused.
Examine sub-section (2) prescribing death or natural life imprisonment for life-convicts who cause hurt in an attempt to murder.
Understand the locus poenitentiae doctrine and the test for criminal attempt.
enhancement.definition: BNS s. 109 penalizes attempt to murder: whoever does any act with such intention or knowledge, and under such circumstances that, if he by that act caused death, he would be guilty of murder, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description up to ten years and fine (sub-section 1); and if hurt is caused by such act, with imprisonment for life or up to ten years and fine; sub-section (2) provides that if a person under sentence of life imprisonment causes hurt in an attempt to murder, they may be punished with death or imprisonment for the remainder of natural life.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Criminalizes proximate acts committed with homicidal intent or knowledge capable of causing death, punishing the execution of the murderous design even when the victim miraculously survives.
statutoryFramework: Chapter VI — Of Offences Affecting the Human Body, BNS s. 109 (corresponding to IPC s. 307).
Sub-section (1) Basic tier: Act done with intention/knowledge that if death ensued would be murder — imprisonment up to ten years, and fine.
Sub-section (1) Hurt tier: If hurt is caused to any person by such act — imprisonment for life, or imprisonment up to ten years, and fine.
Sub-section (2) Life-convict tier: If the offender is under sentence of imprisonment for life and hurt is caused — punishable with death or imprisonment for remainder of natural life.
Statutory illustrations: Firing a gun at someone with intent to kill (illustration a); planting a bomb (illustration b).
essentialIngredients: The act was done with such intention or knowledge, and under such circumstances, that if death were caused, it would amount to murder.
The act was proximate to the intended result and went beyond mere preparation.
For enhanced penalties: Hurt was caused to the victim; or the accused was under sentence of life imprisonment.
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 109 penalizes the inchoate crime of attempt to murder. The prosecution must prove that the accused performed an overt physical act with the intention or knowledge requisite for murder under Section 101. The act must be capable of causing death in the natural and ordinary course of events, though failure may result from outside intervention, defective weapons, or medical rescue. The law does not require that the injury inflicted be fatal or even grievous: shooting at someone with intent to kill and missing completely is an attempt to murder punishable with up to ten years imprisonment. If the bullet grazes the victim causing even simple hurt, the punishment escalates to imprisonment for life. Under sub-section (2), a life-convict who causes hurt in an attempt to murder can be sentenced to death or natural life imprisonment.
examples: Teaching example (Shooting and missing): An accused ambushes his rival, aims a loaded revolver at his head from close range, and pulls the trigger with intent to kill. The bullet misses by inches and strikes a wall. The accused is guilty of attempt to murder under s. 109(1) (up to ten years).
Teaching example (Hurt caused): The bullet strikes the victim's shoulder, causing a flesh wound. Because hurt was caused, s. 109(1) second tier applies (up to life imprisonment).
distinctions: Attempt to murder (s. 109) vs Attempt to commit culpable homicide (s. 110): Section 109 requires the intent/circumstances of murder; Section 110 applies where the act if successful would have been culpable homicide not amounting to murder.

Attempt to murder (s. 109) vs Grievous Hurt (s. 117): Grievous hurt penalizes the severity of the injury caused without homicidal intent; Section 109 focuses primarily on the homicidal intent regardless of injury severity.
problemApplication: Issue: Whether an accused who slashed a victim's throat with a surgical blade, which was saved by emergency surgery, is liable for attempt to murder.
Rule: Doing an act with intent to kill that causes bodily injury capable of causing death constitutes attempt to murder with hurt under BNS s. 109(1).
Application: Slashing a vital organ with a deadly weapon demonstrates homicidal intent, and hurt was caused.
Conclusion: The accused is guilty under BNS s. 109(1) and liable to imprisonment for life.

Explain that fatal injury is not required; homicidal intent and act suffice.

keyTakeaways: Penalizes acts done with homicidal intent or knowledge that fall short of causing death.
Basic attempt without hurt: up to ten years imprisonment and fine.
Attempt where hurt is caused: imprisonment for life or up to ten years and fine.
Life-convict causing hurt: punishable with death or natural life imprisonment.
